findings.quote: 3. **Subscribe.** Shield Advanced protects resources [explicitly specified in Shield Advanced](../facts/shield.md#shield-advanced-not-automatic-per-resource).
findings.evidence: The chapter never says which resources Shield Advanced can protect, yet question q002 (Question 5) offers "add the Elastic IP addresses of the Network Load Balancer as protected resources" and the brief's trap truth (edge-protection-trap-waf-on-any-resource) says a Network Load Balancer is protected by "Shield Advanced ... through its Elastic IP addresses". Fact shield-advanced-resource-types (docs/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-summary-protected-resources): "Amazon EC2 instances, through association to Amazon EC2 Elastic IP addresses.", "Network Load Balancers, through associations to Amazon EC2 Elastic IP addresses.", "AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerators." FREQUENCY.md row 29 lists "Shield Advanced" as a commonly asked topic, and "DDoS protection for EC2 or NLB" is the classic split against AWS WAF. Fix: add one line to step 3 with this list, and a signals row "DDoS protection for an EC2 instance or a Network Load Balancer | Shield Advanced on its Elastic IP | but not if: SQL injection: AWS WAF on an ALB".
findings.resolution: fix-08: Shield step 3 adds [Network Load Balancers, through associations to Amazon EC2 Elastic IP addresses.] (shield-advanced-resource-types). No signals row: the table is fixed at 6 rows.

findings.quote: **Deciding question:** Are DDoS experts and cost protection worth a monthly fee for a year?
findings.evidence: The Shield Standard or Shield Advanced table has no row for cost protection, although the deciding question names it, and no row for what Advanced bundles. Verified facts: shield-cost-protection-credit (service credit), shield-advanced-waf-included (Shield Advanced "includes certain AWS WAF usage for Shield protected resources at no additional cost for up to 50 billion AWS WAF requests per month"), shield-srt-needs-business-or-enterprise-support ("To use the services of the SRT, you must also be subscribed to the Business Support plan or the Enterprise Support plan."). The last one is why question q007 (Question 7) says "The company has an AWS Enterprise Support plan"; nothing in the chapter explains that clue, so the reader reads it as noise. Fix: add rows "Credit for scaling charges | No | Yes", "AWS WAF fees for protected resources | You pay | Included", and in the Help row "Shield Response Team (needs Business or Enterprise Support)".
findings.resolution: fix-08: Shield table: credit row ([request a Shield Advanced service credit]) and the support-plan condition in the help row. The WAF-fees-included row was not added (1-fast word limit).

findings.quote:
- AWS Shield Standard, which is already active for the distribution
- AWS Shield Advanced, after the company subscribes and adds the distribution
- AWS WAF, after a web ACL with a rate-based rule is associated
- AWS Network Firewall, after a firewall is deployed in the origin VPC
findings.evidence: The stem requires protection "without a new subscription or new configuration"; three options say "after ..." a subscription or configuration and only the key says "already active", so the answer is found by matching words, not by knowing Shield. The question also has no qualifier word. Real exam options are parallel. The verified question q008 (status verified, verification pass, difficulty 2) tests the Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy that the signals table and the decision record rely on (Global policy for CloudFront plus one per Region), and no shipped question tests it. Fix: make q006's options parallel (four service names with no state clause), or ship q008 in place of q012 (see exam-07) so Firewall Manager's WAF use has a question; keep the difficulty mix (SPEC difficulty_mix 0.2/0.55/0.25, tolerance 0.1).
findings.resolution: fix-08: q006 set back to verified; the verified question q008 (Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy: Global plus one per Region; core, difficulty 2) ships in its place. q lint --ship clean; difficulty mix 1/7/2 is a warning only.

findings.quote: - Add security group rules and network ACL rules that inspect the domain names and the content of the traffic.
findings.evidence: The option describes a feature that security groups and network ACLs cannot have, in words that announce it ("inspect the domain names and the content"), so nobody picks it; the same option is in the twin q005. Similar self-refuting options: q010 "Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the internet gateway", q012 "Create an AWS WAF web ACL ... and associate it with each EC2 instance". Each question then works as a three-option item. A plausible distractor carries a named misconception: for q001 "Add an outbound security group rule that allows only the IP addresses of the update servers" (misconception: fixed IP lists track domain names; fact well-architected-sec05-finer-control-services) or "Use Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall to block SQL injection".
findings.resolution: fix-08: New distractors change the options of verified questions and need a fresh blind verification (R5); not done in fix. Recorded for the W14 whole-book review.

findings.quote: | "inspect traffic between VPCs" | Network Firewall with a transit gateway | [control and visibility of VPC-to-VPC traffic](../facts/network-firewall.md#network-firewall-when-to-use) | a volumetric DDoS flood: AWS Shield |
findings.evidence: "But not if" should name the small change in the same stem that flips the answer; a volumetric DDoS flood is a different stem. The near-miss the exam actually uses is third-party appliances: FREQUENCY.md section 2 row 6, "third-party firewall appliances → GWLB". Fact network-firewall-uses-gwlb-internally ("AWS Network Firewall already uses AWS Gateway Load Balancer to provide elastic scalability for the firewall endpoint") gives the bridge. Fix: "but not if: the company must keep its own third-party firewall appliances: Gateway Load Balancer" (link the GWLB fact of the ELB chapter or request one).
findings.resolution: fix-08: But-not-if now 'third-party firewall appliances: Gateway Load Balancer'.

findings.quote: > **Changed recently:** (2024-08-30) Lowest request limit of a rate-based rule.
findings.evidence: RULINGS rule 7: where a fact changed since mid-2022, add a Changed recently note. The chapter shows values or names whose verified change facts have no note: waf-change-rate-window-2024 ("configure the time window ... to 1, 2, 5, or 10 minutes. The default is 5, which was the only option before this release.", February 28, 2024; the B-list shows "5 minutes" as the default, and older questions assume a fixed window), waf-change-web-acl-wcu-5000-2023 (April 11, 2023; the B-list shows 5,000 WCUs; older material says 1,500, and fact shield-advanced-waf-included still uses "default (1,500) WCU limits" for pricing), waf-change-protection-pack-console-2025 (June 17, 2025; the text uses the new name), and waf-classic-end-of-support ("AWS WAF Classic | October 7, 2025 | October 7, 2026"; older questions name AWS WAF Classic). Fix: add the rate window note (old: fixed 5 minutes; now: 1, 2, 5 or 10) and the protection pack name note; mention WAF Classic's end of support in one line.
findings.resolution: fix-08: Rate-window Changed recently entry added (see claims-11). WCU and WAF Classic notes not added: 1-fast is at its callout maximum.

findings.quote: A Firewall Manager security group policy can [Audit security group rules](../facts/firewall-manager.md#firewall-manager-sg-policy-three-uses) to find and fix noncompliant rules
findings.evidence: Question 10 tests a security group policy that audits and remediates rule content, but the review section it points to names "security group" only as one policy type ("Each policy is [specific to the individual policy type]: AWS WAF, security group, Network Firewall and others.") and never says what a security group policy does. The only remediation content is FAQ 4 (manual remediation). Fix: either add one step to the Firewall Manager subsection (facts firewall-manager-sg-policy-three-uses, firewall-manager-audit-or-auto-remediate), or ship q008 (Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy, which the subsection and the decision record do teach) in place of q012.
findings.resolution: fix-08: Firewall Manager Write step: a security group policy can also [Audit security group rules] (firewall-manager-sg-policy-three-uses), so q012 is taught.

findings.quote: > **Exam trap:** A per-IP limit can block real users. Staff behind one office address share one count, because the rule counts [based on the request IP address](../facts/waf.md#waf-rate-based-default-key-ip). <!-- trap: edge-protection-trap-per-ip-rate-limit-stops-all -->
findings.evidence: The box carries the trap id whose belief in brief.json is "A rate-based rule that limits each IP address stops every automated sign-in attack." and whose truth is "an attack spread over many addresses can stay under the limit". The box teaches a different point (shared office addresses). The common belief is the one the exam punishes (questions q004 and q003's twin); the shared-address point is a tuning note. Fix: make the box state the belief and the truth: "A per-IP rate limit does not stop an attack spread over many addresses: each address is counted on its own. Use the ATP managed rule group." Move the office-address sentence to the Trade-off or a Go deeper block.
findings.resolution: fix-08: Trap box now states the belief and truth: a per-IP limit misses an attack from many slow addresses; use the ATP group. The office-address point moved out (Trade-off keeps tuning for shared addresses).

findings.quote: 3. **Match.** A statement [inspects for malicious SQL code](../facts/waf.md#waf-sqli-statement-inspects-malicious-sql), an IP set or a country.

findings.quote: The company must stop the flood as soon as possible without blocking real users. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?
